title: QPACK RFC 9204 Foundation Verification
verification_method: Focused requirement-home tests, QPACK milestone and instruction-stream tests, HTTP/3 QPACK error-matrix and integration tests, advisory local h3spec subset evidence, QPACK primitive benchmark Dry validation, SpecTrace JSON validation, and diff hygiene for the RFC 9204 QPACK floor.
scope: This verification covers the standalone QPACK floor: prefixed integers, string literals, the static table, field-section encoding and decoding, dynamic-table accounting, blocked-stream synchronization, and incremental encoder/decoder instruction parsing. It does not verify HTTP/3 request/response semantics or runtime stream-state capture/restore behavior in the HTTP/3 layer.
preconditions: The repo remains in the JSON-only SpecTrace workflow.
The QPACK module stays standalone and does not depend on Incursa.Quic.
expected_result: The focused QPACK tests pass, the requirement-home tests confirm trace linkage for the standalone RFC 9204 floor, core SpecTrace JSON validation accepts the new artifacts, and no whitespace hygiene issues are introduced.
status_summary: The standalone QPACK implementation is trace-owned by canonical RFC 9204 artifacts and is covered by focused milestone, instruction-stream, error-matrix, and HTTP/3 integration tests. The primitive proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9204-S2-0001` directly covers classified positive raw and Huffman string literal decoding, negative malformed prefixed-integer and string-literal encodings, and edge coverage for boundary prefixed integers plus static-table first/last/out-of-range lookups; `QPackPrimitiveBenchmarks` provides a permanent BenchmarkDotNet surface for integer, string-literal, and static-table hot paths. The field-section proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9204-S5-0001` now explicitly classifies positive static/literal-name encode/decode cases, negative truncated literal field-line decoding, and edge cases for duplicate field-line preservation plus deterministic output. The dynamic-state proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9204-S6-0001` now explicitly classifies positive dynamic table insertion, blocking, unblocking, instruction-stream synchronization, negative malformed dynamic references/instructions, peer QPACK decoder-stream parsing in the HTTP/3 server adapter, peer critical-stream EOF mapping to `H3_CLOSED_CRITICAL_STREAM` in local loopback, and edge capacity, eviction, partial-buffer, and blocked-stream-limit behavior. On 2026-06-19, focused local decoder-stream verification passed `dotnet test tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.PeerQPackDecoderStream_ZeroInsertCountIncrement|FullyQualifiedName~QPackInstructionStreamTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3QPackErrorHandlingMatrixTests"` with 35/35 tests, and the advisory local h3spec subset run `.artifacts/http3-h3spec/20260619T0340Z-slice2-http3-qlog` reported the QPACK decoder Insert Count Increment zero case passing while preserving two remaining mapped failures; the report SHA256 is `319619DE246B7EE294B8ED04A2FB954408F119CA9161680CC09068146E4F21D6` and the results SHA256 is `229870729898F80F1B21F2412C19397B40C2FCD7D7C1CFACD445B85A3FB99165`. Focused critical-stream verification passed `dotnet test tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.PeerControlStream_ClosedAfterSettings|FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.PeerQPackDecoderStream_Closed|FullyQualifiedName~Http3MinimalServerTests.PeerQPackDecoderStream_ZeroInsertCountIncrement|FullyQualifiedName~QPackInstructionStreamTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3QPackErrorHandlingMatrixTests|FullyQualifiedName~Http3StreamDispatcherTests"` with 65/65 tests. The qlog-retained h3spec subset `.artifacts/http3-h3spec/20260619T0645Z-qpack-boundary-http3-qlog` reduced the 15-case HTTP/3-matched subset to one RFC 9204 residual: QPACK 4.2 reported transport `STREAM_STATE_ERROR` / `No such stream for MAX_STREAM_DATA` while the server qlog records `http3:error` `ClosedCriticalStream`; the report SHA256 is `A58EF1B588E498230B0F04AC1C4E567B3B8A8B8A4F64878A38BC89ED0427626D` and the results SHA256 is `F14C06A0E9D7B12A692E16662FB4F6EFCABC5500FD22FD71D4BFDDD8CB606041`. The adjacent RFC 9000 requirement coverage `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-1276` continues to require `STREAM_STATE_ERROR` for `MAX_STREAM_DATA` on receive-only streams, and focused h3spec match attempts under `.artifacts/http3-h3spec/20260619T0735Z-qpack-closed-critical-focused-qlog` and `.artifacts/http3-h3spec/20260619T0740Z-qpack-closed-critical-focused-qlog` selected zero cases through the acquired Docker wrapper; those zero-case artifacts are match/tooling diagnostics, not conformance evidence. The remaining QPACK 4.2 h3spec residual is advisory h3spec/tooling interaction unless a new peer trace shows the server mishandling a send-capable stream. On 2026-06-10, BenchmarkDotNet Dry validation for `*QPackPrimitiveBenchmarks*` completed successfully with six cases and `*QPackFieldSectionBenchmarks*` completed successfully with five cases; those Dry runs prove the benchmark surfaces compile and execute but are not performance evidence or a public benchmark claim. Runtime HTTP/3 stream-state capture and restore work remains a separate layer concern.
